result.title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track
result.summary: Forces and torques drive human motion, central to biomechanics, robotics, and physics-aware animation, yet they are often absent from learning-based motion pipelines for body reconstruction and generation. Some motion datasets provide force annotations, but the paired motion sequences are incompatible with the parametric body models used in modern learning pipelines. In addition, existing datasets typically obtain joint torques through inverse dynamics, which is inherently sensitive to the quality of the input kinematics; however, they do not quantify the reliability of these torque estimates. We close this gap with ForceBody, the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-sample torque uncertainty. ForceBody pairs the SKEL body model with ground reaction forces and inverse-dynamics joint torques across 10,386 motion trials (9.7M frames, 26.9 hours) from 140 subjects. Each torque label is paired with a per-frame, per-joint uncertainty annotation obtained by Monte Carlo sampling through the inverse dynamics pipeline. We benchmark six architectures (MLP, Conv1D, LSTM, GRU, Mamba2, Transformer) on ground reaction force and joint torque prediction from SKEL motion. As one example use of the released uncertainty, finetuning a Transformer with per-sample uncertainty weighting reduces the MAE of joint torque estimation by 5%. Code and data are at https://github.com/DominoAI-Lab/ForceBody-NeurIPS-ED-2026.

AI.brief_summary: 论文发布 ForceBody 数据集，将 SKEL 参数化人体模型与地面反作用力、逆动力学关节力矩配对，并为每个力矩标签提供基于 Monte Carlo 采样的逐帧逐关节不确定性，同时基准测试六种架构的预测表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「标签可靠性标注 + 按样本不确定性加权训练」的做法，可能与 LVR 中对 latent 监督的可信度加权、贡献分配有形式上的可借鉴之处，但领域相隔较远，需核查其收益是否来自不确定性本身。
